Late in an unusual lull, an early surprise arose while the duty planner was handling it Companion Animal Travel Desk Incident Report

The duty planner was reviewing the companion animal manifest when a traveler advised that a pet crate was not present at the handover point. The area was calm, and the omission was noticed before boarding activities began in earnest, which helped keep the situation orderly. The traveler remained composed, and the pet was kept safely with the welcome team while the report was opened and the immediate check was started.

The planner first confirmed the intended routing, then compared the manifest against the transfer notes and the baggage intake record. <<FACT F118>> The records showed that the crate had been accepted at an earlier point in the journey, so the desk treated the matter as a recovery and tracing matter rather than a boarding disruption. A careful search was requested through the arrival bay, the sorting area, and the adjacent transfer space. Staff were asked to keep communication plain and reassuring so the traveler received clear guidance without confusion.

Shortly afterward, the crate was identified with the misrouted baggage from an earlier connection and was brought back under escort. The crate remained secure, intact, and correctly labeled. The pet was not exposed to unnecessary movement, and no welfare concern was observed. The traveler was informed at once, and the handover was completed in a controlled manner with a final check of the latch, the label, and the comfort items.

After the incident was resolved, the duty planner recorded the sequence in the operations log and notified the ramp liaison that the sorting step had contributed to the delay in recovery. The follow-up action was to reinforce label verification at transfer points and to remind staff to separate companion animal items from general loose baggage during busy handoffs. The desk also reviewed the communication notes used for the traveler to ensure they stayed concise, kind, and actionable. The incident was contained without escalation, and the companion animal continued travel safely under normal supervision.
